correctness.rationale: Every element of S² annihilates S on either side since S³={0}; conversely any table on A×A with entries in B extends associatively by zero. The requirement S²=B is exactly occurrence of each nonzero label in the table; zero is already produced by products involving B. The size bound gives positive covered mass. With t available labels the diagonals contribute t^r, and equality and inequality pairs contribute t and t(t-1), respectively; inclusion–exclusion gives both displayed counts, including t=1. The unconditioned equality events concern disjoint pairs of entries, giving independent Bernoulli(1/b) variables. The distance to conditioning on coverage is its failure probability, bounded by the union bound; passing to graphs cannot increase distance. Products with B commute, so central generators are exactly the universal vertices. The union bound r b^(-(r-1)) applies before conditioning, with the stated extra TV error. For b=floor(r/(log r+c)), r/b=log r+c+O((log r)^2/r), and both errors vanish. The h-th factorial moment of isolated vertices uses precisely h(r-h)+h(h-1)/2 absent edges and tends to exp(-hc). Components with size k≤r/(log r)^2 have summed tree-and-cross-edge bound O(p) because (1-p)^(r-k)≤C/r; for larger k≤r/2 the cross-edge event alone has bound r^(-k/3). This proves the transfer to the ordinary noncentral graph. Adjoining B preserves closure and commutativity, giving the maximal clique correspondence. Independent small-table enumeration checked six parameter pairs, including the coverage boundary (2,5), the actual multiplication center, and direct commutative subsemigroup enumeration for the two-generator cases.
residual_risks: The supplied checker computes b+clique number rather than independently enumerating maximal commutative subsemigroups, a narrower check than the prose suggests. The all-parameter conclusion follows from the algebraic proof, and the separate two-generator check directly enumerates subsemigroups. No verification for the uniform unlabeled model is implied.

evidence: Dolinka–FitzGerald–Mitchell p. 3 presents maps X×X→K∪{0} whose image contains K; identifying X=A and K=B minus zero is exact.
Araújo–Kinyon–Konieczny p. 1 places the vertices on noncentral elements, whereas the finite F/D count uses the graph on all generators.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The underlying tables are known. Replacing S by a raw product map does not remove coverage conditioning; replacing the noncentral graph by the generator graph requires tracking universal vertices. The inspected background does not give the weighted adjacency law.

evidence: The indexed same-day finding counts 2^(r(r+1)/2) tables per fixed labeling of a graph with no universal vertex, from the minimum-order b=2 case. It gives the G(r,1/2) law conditioned on no universal vertices.
For b=2 and any such graph the all-equal excluded table cannot realize it and F_(r,2)(k)=2^(r+binom(r,2)), which matches that count exactly.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: This is verified same-day special-case coverage without a priority inference. The order-minimal law does not provide the varying-b per-graph counts or the sparse window.

originality.rationale: Credit the standard nilpotent table representation, commuting-graph definition, classical connectivity limit for independent edges, and an indexed special case of the conditional graph count. The surviving claim specifies the graph distribution for arbitrary admissible b and transfers the connectivity window to the noncentral graph in the growing-b semigroup ensemble. The strongest same-day match only treats b=2 without universal vertices. No inspected source contains or determines the general conditioned law and sparse transfer as stated.
residual_risks: The same-day priority relationship for the b=2 special case is unresolved. Grillet's full text and an unindexed equivalent probabilistic formulation remain possible coverage; an unsuccessful focused search is not absence evidence.

value.rationale: Uniform labeled three-nilpotent multiplication is a natural finite algebraic ensemble in which conditioning can distort commutation. The exact graph-frequency invariant quantifies that distortion and handles regimes in which it is not small. The distance estimate then identifies an actual sparse connectivity window for the ordinary noncentral graph, not merely an analogy to independent edges; the clique correspondence connects the law to maximal commutative subsemigroups.
residual_risks: Asymptotic conclusion pertains to fixed labeled sets at each r with the specified growing b, not uniform isomorphism classes or arbitrary size mixtures.
